headline: Of the H-1B applications decided in 2025, 0.6% were denied, down from 10.5% in 2010.
detail: That is 3,457 denials out of 550,769 decisions in 2025, against 34,111 out of 323,489 in 2010. Withdrawn applications count in the total.
how: H-1B applications are the labor condition applications in the Department of Labor's LCA files (case_kind LCA). A denial is a final status of DENIED. The year is the calendar year of the decision date. The total counts every application decided that year: certified, certified then withdrawn, withdrawn and denied. October 2025 has unusually few decisions in the file; without that month the 2025 share is 0.6%. The data does not say why the share fell.

headline: Half of all certified H-1B applications decided from 2010 to 2025 came from 958 employer groups, out of 340,688.
detail: That is 0.28% of employer groups. A group is a normalized employer name, so one company can appear as more than one group.
how: Certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED) decided from 2010 to 2025 with a non-blank employer key: 7,328,281 in all. Employer groups are ranked by application count and added up until they reach half of the total.

headline: In 2025 the average employer group filed 8.5 certified H-1B applications, up from 4.4 in 2010.
detail: Applications rose from 259,107 to 508,147 while the number of employer groups barely moved, from 59,380 to 59,766.
how: Certified H-1B applications decided in each year, divided by the distinct non-blank employer keys among them. An employer key is a normalized-name grouping, not a legal entity.

headline: From 2020 to 2025, 79.4% of certified H-1B applications were decided exactly seven days after they were received, up from 14.4% in 2010 to 2019.
detail: That is 2,355,999 of 2,965,837 applications, against 627,485 of 4,362,446.
how: Calendar days from received_date to decision_date on certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED), grouped by decision year.

headline: About one in three certified H-1B applications decided from 2023 to 2025 was for a software developer.
detail: 489,578 of 1,475,995 applications carry the occupation code 15-1252.00, which the filings label Software Developers.
how: Certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED) decided from 2023 to 2025, grouped on the soc_code field as filed. Seven-character codes such as 15-1252 are completed to 15-1252.00 first, so both spellings of the code are counted.

headline: The median offered wage on certified H-1B applications rose from $66,602 in 2011 to $120,000 in 2025, about 1.8 times as much.
detail: These are nominal dollars, not adjusted for inflation. The offered wage is the wage_from field, the low end of the range stated on the application, converted to a yearly amount.
how: Certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED) decided in 2011 and in 2025. Hourly, weekly, bi-weekly and monthly wages are converted to yearly amounts (x2080, x52, x26, x12). Values below 15,000 or above 1,000,000 a year are dropped, which kept 296,080 applications from 2011 and 506,976 from 2025.

headline: 35.2% of certified H-1B applications decided from 2020 to 2025 offered a wage exactly equal to the prevailing wage.
detail: That is 1,042,042 of 2,963,543 applications, after converting both wages to yearly amounts.
how: wage_from (the wage offered) compared with pw (the prevailing wage stated on the application), both converted to yearly amounts, on certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED). Rows with either value outside 15,000 to 1,000,000 a year are dropped.

headline: 48.9% of certified H-1B applications decided from 2023 to 2025 list a worksite in a different state from the employer's address.
detail: That is 720,426 of 1,473,111 applications. An employer's address is often its headquarters or a filing address, so a difference does not by itself say anything about the application.
how: Certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED) decided from 2023 to 2025 where both the employer state and the primary worksite state map to a state or DC. Applications with several worksites are compared on the primary worksite only.

headline: March's share of the year's H-1B applications fell from 32.5% in 2016 to 9.1% in 2025.
detail: 196,374 of 604,303 applications were received in March 2016, against 48,971 of 538,676 in 2025. October 2025 has almost no applications on record (1,164, against 35,256 in September), which lowers the 2025 total.
how: H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, any status) counted by the month and year of received_date, the date the Department of Labor received them. The data does not say why the timing changed.

headline: Austin, Texas rose from No. 20 to No. 3 among worksite cities for certified H-1B applications between 2012 and 2025.
detail: 2,252 applications in 2012 and 12,551 in 2025. It has been ahead of San Francisco, which had 9,863 in 2025, since 2023.
how: Certified H-1B applications (case_kind LCA, status CERTIFIED) ranked by worksite city and state, with the city name uppercased and trimmed. Only applications whose employer state and worksite state both map to a state or DC are counted. Spelling variants of a city are not merged, so ranks could shift slightly.
